RECOMMENDED LAYOUT FOR TASK 1 ANSWERS
Write an introduction paraphrasing the information provided. If
possible, change the structure from a noun phrase to a noun clause
(change the chart gives information about the number of to the
chart shows how many [..J
Write a clear overview of the main trends, differences, and stages.
If there are trends and differences (ie if there are changes over
time), give some information about both. If there are only
differences, as in questions with no time scale, provide differences
of more than one type.
Put the overview after the introduction in a separate paragraph.
Don't hide it in the introduction or at the end, as it's the first thing
the examiner looks for.
Separate your paragraphs with blank lines. It looks better and there
can be no doubt that it is a new paragraph.
Write one or more paragraphs about the information itself and
organise it logically. Use signposting phrases to show your
organisation to the examiner. Eg Looking first at the most popular

the table gives information about postgraduate course fees across four
subjects and living costs in three countries, A, B, and C.
Overall, courses in countries B and C charged substantially higher fees
than those in country A. Additionally, Computing and Science were the
most expensive courses in all three countries, with country B charging
the highest fees for these two subjects.
Regarding countries B and C, students in country B paid the highest fees,
with 29,000 USD for Science and 27,000 USD for Computing. Similarly,
these two courses also had considerably high fees in country C, at
25,000 USD for the former and 24,000 USD for the latter. As for Arts and
Commerce, students in countries B and C were charged 18,000 USD and
19,000 USD respectively for both courses. Meanwhile, a notable
disparity between the two countries was observed in meals and
accommodation expenses, at 17,000 USD in country B compared to
country C's 11,000 USD.
Turning to country A, it offered the most affordable fees across all
subjects and services. Science and Computing, despite being the most
expensive subjects in country A, cost students 11,000 USD each to
enroll, less than half the corresponding fees in countries B and C. The
lowest fees were charged for the remaining courses, Arts and
Commerce, as well as meals and accommodation, all costing 8,000 USD
each.
